flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: Byzantine fault bound and quorum sizes?
flashcards.a: f faults require N=3f+1 replicas; commit quorum 2f+1. Any two quorums intersect in f+1 nodes, so >=1 honest member in both - conflicting commits cannot both form.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: PBFT phases and its scaling limit?
flashcards.a: pre-prepare -> prepare -> commit, execute at 2f+1; O(n^2) messages and quadratic view change - practical only to ~100 nodes. View change replaces timed-out leader with proof-carrying election.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.a: Leader aggregates votes into threshold-signed quorum certificates: O(n) communication per view, linear view change, pipelined 3-phase commit. Descendants: DiemBFT/Jolteon (Aptos), Narwhal-Bullshark/Mysticeti (Sui ~0.4 s).

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.a: 12 s slots, 32 slots/epoch (~6.4 min), finality after 2 epochs (~12.8 min). Proposer lottery per slot; LMD-GHOST attestation weighting picks head; Casper FFG justifies then finalizes checkpoints at 2/3 stake.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: The three (only) slashable offenses on Ethereum?
flashcards.a: Double proposal (two headers/slot), double vote (conflicting attestations same target epoch), surround vote (illegally nested checkpoint ranges). All produce cryptographic receipts anyone can submit.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.a: Initial: 1/32 of effective balance (<=1 ETH). Correlation: ~min(3 * fraction_slashed_within_4096_epochs, 1) x balance. Solo accident ~1 ETH; coordinated >1/3 attack burns the attackers' entire stake.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: Does being offline get you slashed?
flashcards.a: No - downtime costs missed rewards only (~1:4 ratio vs full participation). Inactivity leak drains offline validators only when finality stalls >4 epochs network-wide, until online remainder regains 2/3.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: Weak subjectivity - one sentence + why PoW doesn't need it.
flashcards.a: PoS nodes must trust a recent checkpoint because old-stake long-range histories are indistinguishable from canonical ones; PoW history is objective since cumulative work can't be fabricated retroactively.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.a: Bitcoin none (depth-based); Ethereum ~12.8 min; Cosmos/Tendermint ~6 s; Aptos ~0.6-1 s; Sui ~0.4 s; Avalanche ~1-2 s (probabilistic safety via subsampled voting).

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: May 2023 mainnet incident - what and lesson?
flashcards.a: Two non-finality episodes (~25 min, ~60 min) from Prysm/Teku bugs splitting attestation weights; blocks kept coming but checkpoints froze. Lessons: client diversity (no >1/3 per client) and justification-gap monitoring, not height alarms.

flashcards.topic: PoW, PoS, BFT: Nakamoto, Finality, Slashing, the Trilemma
flashcards.q: Bitcoin's daily security budget post-2024 halving?
flashcards.a: ~450 BTC/day subsidy (3.125/block) + fees; miners recoup through hardware/energy so attack = outbidding that flow or acquiring un-rentable ASIC majority. Fragility: fee-only sustainability unresolved as subsidy halves each cycle.

flashcards.q: Why would a 20-bank interbank settlement system use classical BFT rather than PoW or PoS?
flashcards.a: Participants are known, small, and accountable -- exactly PBFT's precondition. This gives instant deterministic finality with no energy cost and no probabilistic waiting period, at the cost of needing formal governance for validator-set changes, which the banks already have.
